rule: GOAL: Arrange the slots to match the shown color order. CONTROLS: Click a palette item to select it, click a slot to place or swap, press space to confirm. RULE: The selected item swaps with the slot’s item, and the pushed-out item returns to the palette. TRAP: Thinking the pushed-out item goes to some other palette spot instead of the one you chose.

GOAL: This level required lining up the platform so the released block drops into the target. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the platform; Space released the block. RULE: The block falls only after release, so aim first. TRAP: Thinking the arrows move the block, or that the action bar is only decoration, cost time.

GOAL: Move the object into the gap by using the buttons to open the gray barrier. CONTROLS: The top button moves the upper gray edge one way and the lower gray edge the other way; the bottom button reverses that pair. RULE: The two gray parts are linked, so the buttons open or close the same passage from opposite sides. TRAP: Do not assume clicking moves the object directly; only the barrier shifts, and extra presses can undo progress.

GOAL: Get the purple square to the blue circle. CONTROLS: Clicking a dot moved the square along the line; clicking the circle fed it. RULE: The square only advanced along connected dots, within a short push limit. TRAP: Assuming one far click could carry it all the way.

GOAL: Clear the level by reaching the target in eight arrow moves. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved in four directions; each press was one action. RULE: A move went the distance the game allowed, not the distance you intended. TRAP: Assuming a short move was possible when the game would slide farther.

GOAL: Carry both boxes into the open slots of the container. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; space picks up a box you face or drops a carried box. RULE: A carried box stays at the same distance and direction from you, so lift it facing the way that keeps its path clear. TRAP: Thinking the carried box would shift when you changed facing; it stays fixed, so wrong lifts waste moves.

GOAL: Use arrow presses to make every item match the table clue for its position within the action limit. CONTROLS: Up and down adjust the selected item; left moves the cursor. RULE: The clue chooses the target, and each item follows a fixed cycle, so take the shortest valid turn. TRAP: Do not assume the first visible match is final; check the clue and verify after each press.

GOAL: Fit the plug into the gray shape and clear the level in four clicks. CONTROLS: Each above click moved its part up; each below click moved it down until it stopped. RULE: The colored bar marks the gray edge, and the arrow points into the gray shape. TRAP: Do not assume hidden parts keep a fixed total; test the limit instead.

GOAL: Arrange the tiles so each colored slot holds its matching letter. CONTROLS: Click a tile to select it, click another to swap them, press space to check. RULE: A swap exchanges the two chosen tiles, so a misplaced group must be rotated into place. TRAP: Thinking you could fix one tile at a time; later swaps can undo solved tiles.

GOAL: Guide the ball to the head. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the ball two cells each press. RULE: The key shape showed the only path the ball could follow. TRAP: Thinking a press slides the ball until blocked wasted time.

GOAL: Arrange the pieces so the completed board reads in the hidden order. CONTROLS: Choose a piece, click a slot to place it, then press space to check. RULE: A colored ring marks a nested box; read slots by following the ring colors, left to right within each group. TRAP: Do not assume separate boxes or borders show the order; only matching rings link the groups.

GOAL: Make the red and green slots form one continuous ordered path, then submit. CONTROLS: Click a palette piece to pick it, click a slot to place it, press space to check. RULE: A ring marks where the path enters the connected box, so fill outer, then nested, then remaining outer slots. TRAP: Thinking the ring was just another color, not a connector, cost time.

GOAL: Move the plug off the board in six clicks. CONTROLS: Each click pumps the ball; the water pushes the plug, and the marks show the push pattern. RULE: The plug follows the water, turning or dropping when blocked. TRAP: Thinking the checkerboard pattern was the path wasted time; the water and marks drive it.

GOAL: Get the ball to the waiting head without getting stuck in the narrow passage. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the ball; clicks changed the white switch tiles. RULE: The ball moves two spaces in its facing direction, and the last arrow sets how it settles. TRAP: Thinking the switches or yellow marks had to be handled first; two arrow presses were enough.

GOAL: Turn the row into the target sequence by cycling each slot. CONTROLS: Left and right moved the cursor; up and down cycled the selected shape. RULE: Each mark translated to a fixed run, and the row was those runs joined. TRAP: Believing the row had to be a rearrangement of the target.

GOAL: Arrange tiles so the blue box three tiles repeat twice in the target order, while rings act as wildcards. CONTROLS: Click a palette tile, click a slot to place it, and press space to test the board. RULE: The repeated triplet is the clue; match it to the target list, then use the remaining tiles. TRAP: Treating rings as fixed tiles wastes time; they change where the repeat can sit.

GOAL: reach the exit in three moves by passing through the red hazard after it breaks. CONTROLS: each arrow moved the character that way and ended the turn, letting the hazard act. RULE: the danger came from its lunge, not from touching it; entering broke it. TRAP: believing the red hazard was an unbreakable wall, so testing its tile was avoided.

ESTABLISHED: Blocks on the beam row are locked to it, so vertical beam motion carries every threaded block with the arm. FAILED: Moving the beam, adding blocks, and pulling the line left did not remove or reorder the blocking block. GOAL IS NOT: Not simply clearing the row by sliding threaded blocks off the beam. CONTROLS: Up/down moved the beam; left pulled the packed blocks toward the tip; right pushed them away; adding placed another block on the beam.

GOAL: arrange rings and tiles so the boxes, read in ring order, match the shown sequence. CONTROLS: click a tray piece, click a slot to place it, press space to check. RULE: a ring in the red slots makes its matching box contribute its whole group, and the red slots set the group order. TRAP: thinking the boxes are read in a fixed visual order, or that tray pieces may be left unused.

GOAL: Decode the yellow row into the blue dial row. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows moved the cursor; up arrow turned the selected slot through its cycle. RULE: The yellow row is segmented by the table; the paired blue groups form the target. TRAP: Do not assume the rows match one glyph per slot.

GOAL: Transform the bottom glyphs into the table’s shown targets by following the pair chain. CONTROLS: Arrow keys only; each press moved the selection or advanced the chain. RULE: Each pair teaches how one shape becomes another, and shapes match even when rotated. TRAP: Assuming a glyph had to face the same way wasted time; only its underlying shape mattered.

GOAL: Arrange rings in colored boxes so their traversal order matches the target. CONTROLS: Click one ring to select it, click another to swap them, then press space to check. RULE: The game reads nested boxes depth first, so each ring must sit on the path that produces the target. TRAP: Assuming rings could only stay in their original boxes cost time; they can be swapped into nested slots.

GOAL: Reach the goal without being hit by red enemies. CONTROLS: Each arrow key slides the player that way until blocked. RULE: A red enemy lunges straight ahead within two spaces; landing on it removes it. TRAP: The action budget resets on a new attempt, so failed tries do not reduce it.

GOAL: bring both crosses to the marks that match them. CONTROLS: arrows move the chosen cross; space changes the chosen cross. RULE: one arrow press moves the cross three steps, so count by threes. TRAP: believing a press moves only one step, which makes the plan seem impossible.

GOAL: Make both bars touch their diamond markers. CONTROLS: One control extended a bar toward its marker; the other control retracted it. RULE: The markers, not the shape pair, define success; growth halts at the marker’s edge. TRAP: Believing the facing shapes meant shrink or equal lengths instead of targeting the markers.

GOAL: Get the four corner spaces to show the same color. CONTROLS: Red turned the ring one way; green turned it the other way. RULE: The ring rotated as a whole; success checked the fixed corner spaces. TRAP: Assuming the bright marker meant one special tile had to be placed there.

GOAL: Turn the active panel into the pattern shown in its small preview. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell flips that cell's color; the highlighted panel is the one being edited. RULE: The preview is the target, while the center mark is a fixed clue, not a cell to copy. TRAP: Believing the preview follows the last click or that every visible mark must be changed.

GOAL: This level required routing the rope through the ring, not putting the square inside it. CONTROLS: Clicking moved the head, and the rope dragged along behind it. RULE: The target was judged by the rope, so the connected line was the real moving piece. TRAP: Assuming the square itself had to reach the ring wasted time.

GOAL: Clear the level with two actions, leaving one piece. CONTROLS: Click selected a piece; a second click moved it. RULE: A move only worked by jumping over an adjacent piece into an open space, removing the jumped piece. TRAP: Thinking many actions were required; a short valid move solved it.

GOAL: Align the matching shapes so every target is covered within the move budget. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the selected shape; Space cycled the selected shape. RULE: A target counted only when the matching shape's own lines passed through it; overlap or blocking did not count. TRAP: Thinking you could batch all moves without checking selection or whether the level had already ended.

GOAL: get the needed mark into the matching circle. CONTROLS: arrows move the player; clicks select or activate objects. RULE: the game checks the exact target match, not how many things moved. TRAP: thinking the block must be pushed across the room when one arrow solved it.

GOAL: Make the main grid match the target pattern by turning the needed squares orange and leaving the rest blue. CONTROLS: Clicking a square toggles it between blue and orange; there are no other controls. RULE: The small panels are target stamps: white means orange, green means blue, and overlapping panels must agree. TRAP: Treating the small panels as decoration or as the current board; they show the goal, so wrong clicks must be toggled back.

GOAL: Reach the exit; this level cleared with seven arrow moves. CONTROLS: Each arrow key moves the player one space in that direction. RULE: The exit is satisfied by arrival, not by an extra action. TRAP: Do not assume extra tricks are needed; try the direct arrow path first.

GOAL: Match the hidden pattern on the board; this level took fourteen clicks. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell changed its color; the small windows were clues, not controls. RULE: Each window showed the target: white meant paint, gray meant leave, and overlaps had to agree. TRAP: I wasted time assuming the marker center was already set and ignoring cells no window covered.

GOAL: The level required the two blocks to trade places between the yellow and orange chambers. CONTROLS: Arrows: each arrow moved the blocks in the arrow's direction. RULE: The rule was clear once each block had to reach the opposite color's chamber. TRAP: The trap was assuming the maze was mirror symmetric; it was not.

GOAL: Use six clicks to extend colored bands so the final band covers the marker. CONTROLS: Click a color to extend its band; a blocked color does nothing. RULE: Bands stop at blockers, so thread the chain through the open gap before finishing. TRAP: Believing a blocked click still moves the puzzle; it only wastes an action.

GOAL: This level required moving the selected shapes so their marks cover the target spots and complete the picture. CONTROLS: Arrows move the currently selected shape; Space switches to the next shape. RULE: The selected shape has a blank center, and shapes can overlap without destroying each other. TRAP: Treating that blank center as a missing target cell caused false mismatches and wasted moves.

GOAL: Put every block into its matching socket. CONTROLS: Clicks select blocks; arrow keys move the selected block. RULE: Rings are passable, so blocks can cross or land on them. TRAP: Treating rings as walls wastes moves; do not route around them.

GOAL: Make every white cell under a marker match that marker’s color, while gray cells can be left alone. CONTROLS: A click on a square cycles its color from blue to red to orange to blue. RULE: White cells are required matches; gray cells are only visual context and do not set a color. TRAP: Believing gray cells had to become a hidden third color cost time.

GOAL: Move shapes to cover matching dots with the correct colors. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; space switches shapes. RULE: Any part of a shape touching a slot changes the shape's color, and it keeps that color until another slot changes it. TRAP: Thinking the color disappears when the shape leaves the slot.

GOAL: Move the plug so its red tips match the socket contacts. CONTROLS: Arrow controls moved the whole plug in the pressed direction. RULE: The level cleared when matching colors connected, not when the plug was fully inserted. TRAP: Assuming the plug needed extra sideways movement cost time; alignment was enough.

GOAL: Place each colored tile on its matching colored marker. CONTROLS: Row arrows turned the horizontal loop; column arrows turned the vertical loop; green meant forward, red meant reverse. RULE: The loops were circular and crossed, so a shared tile moved when either loop was turned. TRAP: Assuming the two loops were independent, so one arrow would not disturb the other loop.

GOAL: Make the rope center reach the target while all ropes stay clear. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move the active point; click a point to swap it with the active point. RULE: The center is the average of the three point positions, so only moving a point shifts it. TRAP: Thinking swaps also shift the center; they do not, only moves do.

GOAL: This level asked for a shape match before the timer ran out. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the player piece and made the paired piece move opposite. RULE: The yellow shape was the target, not a second piece to manipulate. TRAP: Assuming every visible shape could be moved cost actions.

GOAL: Solve the level by making the grid match the clues. CONTROLS: Click cross-flip cells to toggle themselves and four neighbors; click clue cells to test them, but they do nothing. RULE: The clues define the target, and only cross-flip cells change the board. TRAP: Assuming all decorated cells are switches; clue cells are inert and cost wasted clicks.

GOAL: move the divider so the reflection reaches the target. CONTROLS: space switched the selection; arrow keys moved the selected object. RULE: the divider mirrors the piece, so moving the divider moves the reflection twice as far. TRAP: assuming the piece itself had to be moved first.

GOAL: Guide the piece so its two tips land on the two marks. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the piece one step at a time. RULE: The fit is clear only when both tips match and the path is free. TRAP: Believing rotation was needed; this solve needed only arrows.

GOAL: This level required one arrow move to complete the target shape. CONTROLS: Arrows move the marker; marked tiles and moving lanes carry it. RULE: The target only appears after the marker lands on the right spots in order. TRAP: Assuming you must walk to the target yourself misses the single move that lets the lane finish.

GOAL: Cover the required dashes with each knot while its space stays clear. CONTROLS: Click a chain point to move the head; click the other point to swap head and anchor. RULE: The knot sits halfway between head and anchor and stays put when you switch chains. TRAP: Thinking you must finish one chain before switching; previous knots remain.

GOAL: Move each shape to its target while carrying the required color. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected shape; Space switches shapes. RULE: The shape takes the color of the last colored area touched by its outline, and keeps it while moving. TRAP: Thinking the final position alone determines the color; the path's last touch decides it.

GOAL: Make the block's top white and bottom purple. CONTROLS: Click selects paint, space pours, arrows move the vat. RULE: Each pour paints only the area under the vat, so use positions whose shapes cover the wanted halves. TRAP: Do not assume you must repaint everything; the current purple may already be the missing half.

GOAL: cover the marked targets with the right pieces so all matches are complete. CONTROLS: arrows moved the selected piece; space changed which piece was selected. RULE: a match only counts when the piece’s shape and facing fit the target, and the color change confirms it. TRAP: thinking one good match or one reflection was enough; the whole set had to match at once.

GOAL: connect all loose ends so the pieces form one linked object. CONTROLS: click selected a piece; arrows moved it; space rotated it. RULE: matching ends that touched turned gray and locked together. TRAP: assuming a rotated piece kept its old position cost time; check where it landed.

GOAL: Put the three yellow tiles into the central slots, then press the center arrow to clear the level. CONTROLS: The outer arrows advance a tile along its own loop; the center arrow only accepts a completed setup. RULE: Each loop can be handled separately, and the order of arrow presses on it does not matter. TRAP: Thinking the top bar was a tight action limit cost time; it did not decrease with normal clicks.

GOAL: Clear the level by sliding loose pieces into their matching marked places. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the currently selected piece; Space changes which piece is selected. RULE: When a piece fits its place, it turns to the completion color, locks, and is skipped by selection. TRAP: Do not assume the last piece you touched is still active; look for the new selection highlight.

GOAL: Use thirteen clicks to place each chain knot on its ring. CONTROLS: Click a free square to move the current head; click a chain point to swap it with the head. RULE: The knot sits at the middle of the chain's three points, so their middle must match the ring. TRAP: Believing colored chain pixels block movement; they usually do not.

GOAL: required solving with only moves that change the final state, not checks. CONTROLS: each control performed its move immediately; there was no safe preview. RULE: opposite moves cancel, so only the net effect matters. TRAP: thinking a test click was harmless; it still spent an action.

GOAL: Reach the target within a strict action budget, using a refill pickup when the direct route would run out. CONTROLS: Arrows move you and spend one action; conveyors carry you; rings restore the action meter. RULE: A longer route can be cheaper if a pickup refills the budget before the final distance. TRAP: Assuming the shortest path is always best; the detour to the ring made the level solvable.

GOAL: add the last orange patch with one bottle drop, after the vat is aimed. CONTROLS: turning the vat aimed the drop; clicking the bottle emptied it. RULE: the bottle rode on the vat, so its landing spot followed the vat's angle. TRAP: assuming the bottle stayed fixed when the vat moved.

GOAL: Reach the head by making the ball face the open path. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate or roll the ball; keypad buttons launch it. RULE: The launch follows the ball's last successful direction, not the last key pressed. TRAP: Treating blocked arrows as harmless; they can rotate the ball and waste moves.

GOAL: Slide one mirror to make the piece's reflection match the target. CONTROLS: Space cycles the selection; arrows move only the selected object. RULE: Mirrors change the reflection directly, so the piece does not need to move. TRAP: Assuming the piece had to be moved first when a mirror shift solved it.

GOAL: Move the knot through the marked zones and into the target area. CONTROLS: Click an open cell to move the head; click an anchor to swap it with the head. RULE: The knot is determined by the head and two anchors, so set the anchors first, then place the head. TRAP: Believing the knot itself can be clicked and moved directly wastes clicks.

GOAL: Get the ball to the target while keeping enough time. CONTROLS: Arrows move the ball; keypad lines launch it along a clear row. RULE: Passing over green restores time, and a launch can consume far targets in line. TRAP: Thinking the launch was required when seven arrow moves already solved it.

GOAL: Make every letter tile show the glyph shapes required by the sentence rows. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tile cursor; up and down change the selected tile. RULE: The mapping comes from the sentence rows, not from the order the cards appear. TRAP: Assuming two-part tiles need separate changes wastes time; the whole tile changes together.

GOAL: Clear the level with only two clicks: choose the final color, then release it. CONTROLS: Clicks selected and applied; arrows moved the vat; space poured. RULE: The final release overwrites the cells it covers, so the last action decides. TRAP: Believing I needed a long move-and-pour route cost time when two clicks cleared it.

ESTABLISHED: This level is unsolved and over budget; linked colored pieces grow, retract, and block. FAILED: Changing nearby pieces to free a blocked retract did nothing. GOAL IS NOT: It is not just matching colors or shrinking the orange piece. CONTROLS: Move shifted pieces; grow extended them; retract failed unless vacated space was clear.

GOAL: Clear the level by making the two blocks pass through each other. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved both blocks as a pair; left and right presses could make them trade places when side by side. RULE: The level ended when the blocks crossed, not when they merely touched. TRAP: Thinking blocks must stop when they touch; they can pass through and swap.

GOAL: Clear the level in eleven arrow presses by pushing the shape into its socket. CONTROLS: Each arrow moved the cursor; pressing toward a shape pushed it along that direction. RULE: Outlines are not solid, so a shape can slide across an outline and still park. TRAP: Assuming the outline would block the slide cost extra moves.

GOAL: Fit the pieces so their mirror images cover every target mark. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; space confirms the placement. RULE: A placement is right only when all reflected copies also land on targets and together fill them. TRAP: Assuming reflections are ghosts; they are real constraints and can spoil a fit that looks correct.

GOAL: reach the exit before the move limit runs out. CONTROLS: each arrow moves the player one space in that direction. RULE: patrolling enemies move after you, so a space is safe only if the guard does not arrive there on that move. TRAP: assuming the shortest route wins; small extra steps can wait out the guard.

GOAL: get the ball into the head. CONTROLS: arrows move the ball; clicks activate teleporters. RULE: the level ends when the ball overlaps the head. TRAP: assuming the teleport slot must match the ball size wastes time.

GOAL: This level required using two avatars to push a plus block into its socket. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active avatar; clicking switched control to the other avatar. RULE: A pushed block slides until stopped by a wall or boundary, so plan where it will stop. TRAP: Thinking both avatars could act at once; only the active one could move or push.

ESTABLISHED: RIGHT moves the paddle; the block and cups stay unchanged when SPACE is used. FAILED: Pressing SPACE did not launch the block, and paddle movement alone did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: launching the block into the cups or just aligning the paddle. CONTROLS: RIGHT shifts the paddle sideways; SPACE has no visible effect here.

GOAL: Send every marker on its route, then move the blocks to finish. CONTROLS: Mouse activates a marker; arrows move it; clicking a block deactivates it. RULE: Only one marker can be active, so deactivate before starting the next. TRAP: Leaving a marker active wastes actions and prevents the final block moves.

GOAL: Move the bead to the panel opening, then trigger its peg to jump over the blocking peg and clear the board. CONTROLS: Directional presses slide the bead along the pipe; clicking the bead's peg activates a jump. RULE: A peg can jump over an adjacent occupied position into an empty one, removing the jumped peg. TRAP: Thinking the peg already in the panel was a blocker to avoid, when it was the foothold.

GOAL: Move the character into the open target area. CONTROLS: UP moved up, DOWN moved down, LEFT moved left, RIGHT moved right. RULE: The level cleared when the character reached the empty target area. TRAP: Assuming the colored blocks had to be moved or solved wastes time.

ESTABLISHED: A small action bar empties and resets the level, so every click must change the board. FAILED: Empty clicks, overlaps, and actions after the bar was low wasted time or reverted. GOAL IS NOT: Not just moving one piece to a target or making pieces touch; that did not clear. CONTROLS: Clicks move the nearest valid piece; nearby same-size pieces may merge, invalid moves fail.

GOAL: Reach the exit without being caught by the moving patrollers. CONTROLS: Each arrow key moved the player one step in that direction. RULE: The patrollers followed fixed straight paths and bounced at the ends, so safe timing could be planned. TRAP: Assuming a horizontal patroller moved vertically; that wrong belief made the first plan unsafe.

GOAL IS NOT: Just filling all box slots, because the orange also needs to cover one. CONTROLS: Arrows move, Space places the held box, and the orange moves between turns.

ESTABLISHED: Fixed pieces already link one pair of ends; the loose pieces must chain the two open ends. FAILED: Trying many loose-piece orientations without checking the whole connection burned extra cost and did not clear. GOAL IS NOT: The goal is not to make each loose piece touch a fixed piece; they must connect to each other in the missing chain. CONTROLS: Rotation changes endpoint spacing, dragging moves a piece, and contact registers when ends meet or touch edge to edge.

GOAL: Deliver every box into the container's open slots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; Space picks up or drops a box. RULE: A box counts only if it remains on an open slot after the player moves away. TRAP: Do not count a slot as filled just because a carried box covers it.

CONTROLS: Arrows move or bump the player; Space picks up or places a box; each action advances the companion.
